answer: An agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake bond before it may trade, with the bond held in escrow and slashed if the agent is caught cheating. Like a tide that lifts only anchored boats, the bond raises the cost of spawning fake identities: each Sybil copy needs its own stake, so flooding the market drains the attacker capital instead of multiplying influence. A cedar grows slowly and a cipher proves its key, so reputation accrues only to identities with a long, verifiable history of honest work, making cheap throwaway copies worthless.
